figures.finding: In Saint Vincent and the Grenadines a child (under fourteen) shall not be employed, save in the Act's Part I work, light farm or garden work for a parent out of school hours, and taking part without fee or reward in an entertainment whose proceeds go to charity, education or another non-profit purpose; so a child can't be paid to perform, and no permit exists (reading); the bar is general and reaches any paid work, writing or directing too.

value.performerException: unpaid charitable or educational entertainment only

figures.applies: Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, Cap. 209 (revised edition 2009) ss. 2, 8, copy in the University of the West Indies (Cave Hill) law library's UNICEF database.

sources.said: "child" means a person under the age of fourteen; ... (1) Subject to subsection (2), a child shall not be employed. (2) Nothing in subsection (1) applies— ... (c) to the participation of a child, without fee or reward, in an entertainment the net proceeds of which are devoted to any charitable or educational purpose or to any purpose other than the private profit of the promoters.

figures.finding: A person attains full age at eighteen in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines; how a minor's contract binds and any set-aside of earnings were not found (see blockers).
figures.applies: Age of Majority Act, Cap. 226 s. 2 (UWI Cave Hill copy).

sources.said: (1) As from the 15th September, 1987, a person shall attain full age on attaining the age of eighteen instead of attaining the age of twenty-one
